rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) is not applied for from an authority. You request it from your employer, in text form. The notice period depends on when the leave falls.

- Leave before your child's third birthday: at least seven weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens sieben Wochen").
- Leave between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year: at least 13 weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

The request must be made "in Textform". The federal family portal explains that this can be an email or a letter without a signature.

If you request leave for the period before the third birthday, you must say at the same time which periods within two years you will take as Elternzeit.

The law allows a shorter period in some cases. Where there are urgent reasons, "ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist" (exceptionally, an appropriate shorter period) is possible. The family portal names premature births as one example, and says the period then depends on the individual case.

There is a separate rule for mothers whose Elternzeit is to start directly after the maternity protection period after birth. If a reason outside the mother's control prevents a timely request, she can make it up within one week after that reason ends. Where a mother takes Elternzeit straight after that protection period, the protection period counts towards the two-year period mentioned above.

Your employer must give you written confirmation of your Elternzeit ("Der Arbeitgeber hat ... die Elternzeit zu bescheinigen").

One caution: the family portal says that for children born before 1 July 2015, a seven-week notice period applies even for leave after the third birthday. The transitional provision in the statute behind this is not among the excerpts I have, so I cannot confirm where that boundary lies. If your child was born before that date, check the transitional rule in the BEEG before relying on the 13-week figure.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under the statute, the claim to Elterngeld (parental allowance) lapses above a set zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income).

BEEG §1(8) says the claim lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the entitled person had a zu versteuerndes Einkommen of more than 175,000 euros ("mehr als 175 000 Euro") in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth ("im letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt des Kindes"). If another person also meets the entitlement conditions, the claim lapses when the combined zu versteuerndes Einkommen of both persons is more than 175,000 euros ("die Summe des zu versteuernden Einkommens beider Personen mehr als 175 000 Euro").

The limit refers to zu versteuerndes Einkommen, not gross income. The federal Familienportal explains that gross income is usually considerably higher, because special expenses, provision expenses, allowances and extraordinary burdens are deducted first. It also states that your individual zu versteuerndes Einkommen is determined by the Finanzamt and appears in your tax assessment notice (Steuerbescheid).

If the tax assessment notice for the last completed assessment period is not yet available when you apply, BEEG §8 provides that the decision is made provisionally ("vorläufig"). If the application indicates the limit will likely not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation ("unter dem Vorbehalt des Widerrufs") in case the limit turns out to be exceeded.

The 175,000 euro figure is the one the statute states. The Familienportal guidance says different limits applied to earlier births. The excerpts here do not include the statute's transitional provision, so this answer does not say which limit applies to a birth on a particular date. Which limit applies to your child's birth, and whether you are entitled, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) is a set of extra monthly payments for parents who both work part time at the same time. Under BEEG §4b(1), each parent receives "einen zusätzlichen Monatsbetrag Elterngeld Plus" (an additional monthly amount of ElterngeldPlus) for each month of the child's life in which the conditions are met.

Conditions in the law (BEEG §4b):
- Both parents work "nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats" (at least 24 and at most 32 hours a week, averaged over the month of the child's life).
- Both parents meet the general conditions of BEEG §1. That section is not in the excerpts, so its content is not described here.
- Each parent can receive at most four months of Partnerschaftsbonus, and only if it is taken for at least two months.
- Both parents must take it at the same time and in consecutive months of the child's life.
- If, after the bonus has been applied for, the conditions turn out not to have been met in every month, the consecutive-months requirement still counts as met (§4b(5)).

One parent alone (BEEG §4c(2)): a single parent can receive the extra payments for two to four consecutive months of working 24 to 32 hours a week on average, if one of these grounds applies:
1. the parent meets the conditions for the single-parent tax relief under §24b(1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act, and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child;
2. care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of §1666(1) and (2) of the Civil Code; or
3. care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of a serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count.
If one of these grounds arises while both parents are already receiving the bonus, one parent can continue it alone (§4b(4)).

Amount: the official family portal says the bonus is calculated the same way as ElterngeldPlus and, depending on income before the birth, is between 150 and 900 euros a month per parent. It also says parents who raise their child separately can receive it.

The family portal notes that its explanations cover children born after August 2021. Different rules partly apply to earlier births.

Whether you qualify and how much you would receive is decided only by the parental allowance office for your district.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is 259 euros per month. The law sets the same amount for every child, so the first child gets the same as any other: "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro" (EStG §66 (1); the same wording appears in BKGG §6 (1)).

It is paid monthly from the start of the month in which the conditions are met until the end of the month in which they stop being met (EStG §66 (2)).

This is the amount the law sets. Whether your family is entitled is decided by the authority, not here. The official family portal says the Kindergeld application can be made online with the Bundesagentur für Arbeit.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Not simply because the baby is born here. German law ties citizenship by birth to conditions, and for children of two non-German parents those conditions concern a parent's residence.

The general rule is that a child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) at birth if a parent holds German Staatsangehörigkeit (StAG §4(1): "wenn ein Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit besitzt").

For a child of foreign parents, StAG §4(3) says the child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit through birth in Germany ("Durch die Geburt im Inland erwirbt ein Kind ausländischer Eltern die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit") if at least one parent meets both of these conditions:
1. has lawfully had their habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland hat"), and
2. holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or, as a Swiss national or a family member of one, a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.

The same provision says the acquisition is entered in the birth register in which the child's birth is recorded ("in dem Geburtenregister, in dem die Geburt des Kindes beurkundet ist, eingetragen").

Whether either of you meets these conditions is decided by the responsible authorities, not here. To find out about your own case, approach the registry office that records your child's birth, or your local citizenship authority (Staatsangehörigkeitsbehörde).

If a child born in Germany does not become German, the residence rules in AufenthG §33 apply. A residence permit is issued to the child automatically ("von Amts wegen") if, at the time of birth, both parents hold a residence permit, a settlement permit or an EU long-term residence permit. If only one parent holds such a permit, a residence permit can be issued. Your local Ausländerbehörde is the authority for residence matters.

The excerpts do not cover Indian citizenship for your child. The Indian consular track handles that question.

rows.question: Does our newborn need a residence permit?
rows.reply:
German federal law sets out several situations for a child born in Germany. Which one applies to your child is decided by the authorities, not here.

Residence permit for a child born in Germany (AufenthG §33):
- If one parent holds an Aufenthaltserlaubnis (residence permit), a settlement permit or an EU long-term residence permit, the child born in Germany can be granted an Aufenthaltserlaubnis on the authority's own initiative.
- If, at the time of birth, both parents hold one of these permits, the child is granted the Aufenthaltserlaubnis on the authority's own initiative. The same applies if the parent with sole custody holds one. The statute says "wird ... erteilt" here, meaning it is granted, not just that it can be.
- If the mother or father holds a visa at the time of birth, or may stay in Germany without a visa, the child's stay counts as permitted. This lasts until that visa or that lawful visa-free stay ends.

German citizenship by birth (StAG §4):
- A child acquires German citizenship by birth if one parent is a German citizen.
- A child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German citizenship if one parent meets both of these conditions:
  1. They have lawfully had their habitual residence in Germany for five years.
  2. They hold an unlimited right of residence, or a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement as a Swiss citizen or a family member of one.
- This acquisition is entered in the birth register where the birth is recorded.

The excerpts do not say how citizenship by birth affects the need for a residence permit. They also do not say how the procedure works.

Only the responsible authority decides your child's residence status. For this, approach the local immigration authority (foreigners' office) for your place of residence.

the Ausländerbehörde is the responsible authority

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Bavaria (Bayern) is outside the states this product covers. We cover federal law, Hessen state procedures and the Indian consular track. For Bavarian procedures, such as where to apply and which forms to use, contact the Elterngeld office responsible for your district in Bavaria or the Bavarian state government's official portal.

The Elterngeld (parental allowance) rules themselves are federal law, so the federal rules below apply in Bavaria too.

Who can claim: a person who lives or habitually resides in Germany, lives in one household with the child, cares for and raises the child themselves, and does no work or does not work full time ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt").

Income from self-employment counts. The income used includes positive income from "Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Gewerbebetrieb und selbständiger Arbeit" (farming and forestry, trade or business, and self-employed work), as well as employment income. This income must be taxable in Germany, and taxes and social contributions are deducted from it. Elterngeld is 67 percent of income from work before the birth. This percentage rises for incomes below 1,000 euros and falls, down to 65 percent, for incomes above 1,200 euros. For full months without income from work, the maximum is 1,800 euros a month ("Höchstbetrag von 1 800 Euro monatlich"). The minimum is 300 euros, including for someone who had no income from work before the birth.

Working after the birth: in months where income from work is on average lower than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as the relevant percentage of the difference. For this calculation, pre-birth income counts up to at most 2,770 euros.

Provisional decisions and proof: the amount is decided provisionally, based on credible information, in three cases:
(1) the tax assessment for the last completed tax period before the birth ("Steuerbescheid für den letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt des Kindes") is not yet available, and it cannot yet be said whether the limits in §1(8) are exceeded;
(2) income from work before the birth cannot be determined;
(3) the claimant expects to have income from work during the payment period.

If the application stated expected income from work, the actual income for that period must be proven after the payment period ends. If that tax assessment is missing when you apply, and the application says the limits will probably not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case they are.

Other income received in place of earnings, and some maternity benefits, are deducted from Elterngeld.

Only the responsible Elterngeld office decides any individual entitlement or amount. This answer does not assess your case.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
I can't fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application. The entries on it are decisions about your own case: which months you claim, what income you declare, and which of you claims what. Choosing those for you would mean judging your individual entitlement, which only the responsible authority decides.

What the law says the application involves:

- It must be made in writing: "Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen" (BEEG §7(1)).
- It must state the months for which you claim Basiselterngeld, the months for Elterngeld Plus, and the months for the Partnerschaftsbonus (BEEG §7(1)).
- Payment is backdated only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate" (BEEG §7(1)). Applying later loses earlier months of payment.
- The parent applying signs it. The other entitled parent also signs, to confirm they have seen it. This does not apply in the case of §4c or when one parent alone has custody. The other parent can at the same time make their own application, or tell the authority how many monthly amounts they claim (BEEG §7(3)).
- If you give expected earnings in the application, you must prove your actual earnings for that period once the payment period ends (BEEG §8(1)).
- The decisions you make in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period. Changes reach back only three months, and are not allowed for months already paid out, except in cases of special hardship (BEEG §7(2)).

The federal family portal lists the documents to attach. These are your child's birth certificate and proof of your previous income. For employees, that means pay slips for the last 12 months before maternity protection begins (mothers) or before the birth (fathers). For self-employed people, it is usually the last tax assessment.

Who decides: the competent authority is the one the Land designates for the district where your child has their residence in Germany when you first apply (BEEG §12(1)). The family portal calls this "Ihre Elterngeldstelle". That office decides your application, and it is where you can raise questions about how to complete it.

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
Whether your application will be approved is decided only by the responsible authority. It is not something this service can assess or predict. Here is what the law says.

Under BEEG §1(1), a person is entitled to Elterngeld (parental allowance) if they meet all four of these conditions:
1. they have a residence or habitual abode in Germany ("einen Wohnsitz oder seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt in Deutschland"),
2. they live in one household with their child,
3. they care for and bring up this child themselves, and
4. they are not working, or not working full-time ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt").

For multiple births there is only one entitlement.

BEEG §1 also sets out further groups who can be entitled:
- §1(2): some people who do not meet condition 1. This covers people subject to German social insurance law under §4 SGB IV, public servants temporarily posted abroad, development workers and certain missionaries, and German nationals working temporarily at an international organisation. Spouses living in the same household are covered too.
- §1(3): some people who do not meet condition 2 in the usual way. This covers a child taken in with the aim of adoption, a spouse's child taken into the household, and a recognition or determination of paternity that is not yet effective or decided.
- §1(4): relatives up to the third degree and their spouses, where the parents cannot care for the child because of serious illness, severe disability or death.

Under BEEG §7(1), Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("ist schriftlich zu beantragen"). It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

Which of these conditions your family meets, and whether your application is approved, is decided by the Elterngeld office for your district.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
How much tax you would save by changing tax class is a tax calculation for your household. This service cannot work that out or say whether the switch is worth it. Questions about tax effects and tax class choice belong to your tax office or a tax adviser.

What the excerpts do say is how a tax class change before the birth is treated when parental allowance is calculated:

- Parental allowance is based on a simplified net income figure. For this, "kommt es auf die neueste Steuerklasse an": the most recent tax class is used.
- The older tax class is used only if it applied for longer than the newer one across the whole assessment period ("wenn diese innerhalb des gesamten Bemessungszeitraums länger gegolten hat als die neuere").
- The income tax deduction takes account of the tax class and, where one applies, the factor under §39f of the Income Tax Act. Tax class VI is disregarded ("die Steuerklasse VI bleibt unberücksichtigt").
- Changing tax class again after the birth has no further effect on parental allowance ("hat also keine Auswirkung mehr auf Ihr Elterngeld").

Only the parental allowance office for your district decides which tax class is used in your case and what amount you receive. For the tax side, contact your local tax office or a tax adviser.
